claims.text: High configurational entropy is a primary governor of structural and chemical stability in near-equiatomic multi-element solid-solution nanoparticles at high temperature.
Local chemical ordering is a primary governor of structural and chemical stability in these nanoparticles.
Local chemical ordering creates large energy barriers to atomic diffusion.
The barriers associated with local chemical ordering suppress phase segregation.
The barriers associated with local chemical ordering suppress nanoparticle sintering.
Trace impurities perturb locally ordered atomic environments.
Trace oxygen or nitrogen impurities can promote phase decomposition during thermal aging.
Multi-element solid-solution nanoparticles can be synthesized as a single phase.
The proposed initial nanoparticles are chemically homogeneous and contain minimal extrinsic impurities.
Processing conditions can be adjusted to promote or diminish local chemical ordering.
Local chemical ordering relevant to stability is encoded by an effective phase diagram.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a disordered but homogeneously mixed phase.
Impurities above a critical concentration disrupt diffusion barriers created by local order.
Interstitial impurities can promote phase segregation during high-temperature aging.
Impurities can promote nanoparticle sintering during high-temperature operation.
High-purity nanoparticles with robust local chemical ordering will retain a single-phase solid-solution structure during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Increasing impurity content will cause earlier phase segregation during thermal exposure.
Increasing impurity content will cause nanoparticle coarsening during thermal exposure.
The critical impurity concentration or local-order threshold varies with elemental composition and processing history.
The hypothesis may cease to be valid when impurity levels exceed the critical threshold.

contradictions.description: The mechanism specifically predicts that impurities above a critical threshold disrupt local-order barriers and cause instability, whereas the boundary states that the hypothesis itself may lose validity above that same threshold.
